```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggpubr)
library(dplyr)
library(emmeans)
library(interactions)
library(lmtest)
library(car)
library(performance)
library(datawizard)
library(lmerTest)
library(lme4)
library(ggeffects)
```

```{r}
df <- read.csv('Contextualisation_Scores_R.csv')
df <- df[which(df$Dataset =='1'),]

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    Score = case_when(
      Factor == "F1" & Type == "N" ~ Score / 5,
      Factor == "F1" & Type == "C" ~ Score / 6,
      Factor == "F2" ~ Score / 3,
      TRUE ~ Score
    )
  )

unique(df["Participant"])

```

```{r}
#Let's preprocess our relevant features
df$Factor <- as.factor(df$Factor)
df$Participant <- as.factor(df$Participant)
df$Dataset <- as.factor(df$Dataset)
df$Type <- as.factor(df$Type)
df$CERF <- factor(df$CERF, 
                          levels = c('A1', 'A2', 'B1', 'B2', 'C1', 'C2'), 
                          ordered = TRUE)
df$Feature <- as.factor(df$Feature)
df$Word.Frequency.stand <- standardize(df$Word.Frequency)
df$AoA.stand <- standardize(df$AoA)
df$Word.Length.stand <- standardize(df$Word.Length)
df$Polysemy.stand <- standardize(df$Polysemy)
df$Understandability.Score.log <- df$Score

```

```{r}
#Really simple model
model <- lmer(Understandability.Score.log ~ Factor + Word.Frequency.stand + Factor*Word.Frequency.stand + (1 + Factor | Participant) + (1 | Feature), data = df)
summary(model)

check_heteroscedasticity(model)  # Checks for equal variance
check_normality(model)           # Checks if residuals are normal
check_collinearity(model)

#Check q-q plot to see if non-normality is actually a problem
qqnorm(residuals(model), main = "Q-Q Plot of Residuals", pch = 16, col = "darkgray")
# Add the reference line
qqline(residuals(model), col = "red", lwd = 2)

# Make sure the interactions package is loaded
library(interactions)

# 1. Test the significance of the slopes for each level of Factor
sim_slopes(model, 
           pred = Word.Frequency.stand, 
           modx = Factor, 
           johnson_neyman = FALSE)

# 2. Plot the interaction lines
my_interaction_plot <- interact_plot(model, 
              pred = Word.Frequency.stand, 
              modx = Factor, 
              plot.points = TRUE,
              x.label = "Word Frequency (z-scores)",
              y.label = "Understandability") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("F1" = "blue", "F2" = "red")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("F1" = "blue", "F2" = "red"))

ggsave(filename = "Word Frequency.png", 
       plot = my_interaction_plot, 
       dpi = 300, 
       width = 7, 
       height = 5, 
       units = "in")

interact_plot(model, 
              pred = Word.Frequency.stand, 
              modx = Factor, 
              plot.points = TRUE,
              x.label = "Word Frequency",
              y.label = "Understandability") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("F1" = "blue", "F2" = "red")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("F1" = "blue", "F2" = "red"))
```

```{r}
#Check Word Length next
#Really simple model

#Okay Interaction isn't significant
model <- lmer(Understandability.Score.log ~ Factor + CERF + Factor*CERF + (1 + Factor | Participant) + (1 | Feature), data = df)
summary(model)

#High VIF so let's just drop CERF for now - we can come back to it!

check_heteroscedasticity(model)  # Checks for equal variance
check_normality(model)           # Checks if residuals are normal
# 2. Fit a linear model with the exact same fixed effects structure
# 2. Fit a linear model with the exact same fixed effects structure
temp_lm <- lmer(Understandability.Score.log ~ Factor + CERF + Factor*CERF + (1 + Factor | Participant) + (1 | Feature),, data = df)

# 3. Calculate the generalized VIF
library(car)
vif(temp_lm)

#Check q-q plot to see if non-normality is actually a problem
qqnorm(residuals(model), main = "Q-Q Plot of Residuals", pch = 16, col = "darkgray")
# Add the reference line
qqline(residuals(model), col = "red", lwd = 2)

# 1. Estimate predictions for the combination of CERF and your Moderator
# Note: Place the primary variable (CERF) first in the vector
predictions <- predict_response(model, terms = c("CERF", "Factor"))

plot(predictions) +
  labs(
    x = "CERF Ordered Levels",
    y = "Understandability Cost (log)",
    color = "Factor",
    fill = "Factor" # Keeps the confidence interval shading consistent
  ) +
  # Assign blue to F1 and red to F2
  scale_color_manual(values = c("F1" = "blue", "F2" = "red")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("F1" = "blue", "F2" = "red")) +
  # Custom y-axis limits (zoom from 1 to 3.5)
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 5)) +
  theme_minimal()
# 

library(interactions)
library(ggplot2)

# Generate the categorical interaction plot in the interact_plot style
ip <- plot(predictions) +
  labs(
    x = "CERF Ordered Levels",
    y = "Understandability",
    color = "Factor",
    fill = "Factor" # Keeps the confidence interval shading consistent
  ) +
  # Assign blue to F1 and red to F2
  scale_color_manual(values = c("F1" = "blue", "F2" = "red")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("F1" = "blue", "F2" = "red")) +
  # Custom y-axis limits (zoom from 1 to 3.5)
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 5)) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave(filename = "CEFR_Med.png",
       plot = ip,
       dpi = 300,
       width = 7,
       height = 5,
       units = "in")
```
